points.text: 1) The Imamate — Shi'a Muslims believe God appointed twelve Imams to guide the Muslim community after Muhammad's death. These Imams are infallible and divinely chosen. questions.question: Why do Sunni and Shi'a Muslims have different beliefs?

points.text: The division originated after Muhammad's death in 632 CE over who should lead the Muslim community. Sunni Muslims believed the leader should be chosen by the community (Abu Bakr was selected). Shi'a Muslims believed leadership should pass through Muhammad's family (Ali, his cousin and son-in-law).
